title: account-profile: fix broken DeleteAccountProfile and erase profile data on identity.account.erased
description: DeleteAccountProfile (account-profile/internal/infrastructure/persistence/account_repository.go:276) can never succeed: table 'account_profile' instead of account_profile.profiles, missing comma between 'deleted_at = $2' and 'updated_at', WHERE id instead of account_id. It has no callers. Implement: subscriber for identity.account.erased that, in one tx, explicitly DELETEs (child first, no ON DELETE CASCADE) activity_interests, settings, profile_statistics, account_settings_meta, then profiles; inserts account_profile.erased_account(account_id, erased_at); raises account_profile.account.erased via the outbox. Delete the profile picture file from storage (after commit; retry-safe). Idempotent on redelivery. Decide whether the soft-delete DeleteProfile path stays at all. Integration test.
notes: Erasure confirmation (from dh7.1): identity already subscribes to `account_profile.account.erased` (it is in the default ACCOUNT_ERASURE_CONTEXTS). After erasing this context's data on identity.account.erased, raise `account_profile.account.erased` through the outbox in the same transaction, payload {"event_id", "account_id"} (account_id only, no personal data). Until this ships, identity counts every erasure as incomplete for account_profile after ACCOUNT_ERASURE_INCOMPLETE_AFTER (7d) and AccountErasureIncomplete fires.
close_reason: account-profile erases all account rows on identity.account.erased in one tx, records erased_account, confirms with account_profile.account.erased; late verified events dropped; broken DeleteProfile path removed; integration tests

title: Login: failed attempts and account lockout are rolled back, so lockout never happens
description:
Service.Login (identity/internal/application/service.go ~385-415) records the failed attempt (Account.RecordFailedLoginAttempt: counter, login.failed event, and Lock after 5 attempts = 15 min, 10 = 1 year), then UpdateAccount + InsertEvents, and then returns domain.ErrInvalidCredentials from inside the same WithTransaction callback. WithTransaction rolls back on any error, so the counter, the login.failed event and the account.locked event are never persisted. failedLoginAttempts therefore never reaches 5 and accounts are never locked: no brute-force protection on login apart from the gateway rate limit (found by reading the code, not yet reproduced).

Fix: persist the failure in a transaction that commits, then return ErrInvalidCredentials after it (e.g. run the transaction, remember the error, return it once committed). Consider concurrency: two parallel wrong passwords should both count (lock the account row or increment in SQL). Check that a locked account is rejected on login (Account.IsLocked) and that the counter resets on success.

Tests: integration test through Service.Login: 5 wrong passwords lock the account (login rejected with account_locked even with the right password), counter persists across calls, login.failed events reach the outbox, success resets the counter. identity/internal/application has no tests and uses concrete deps; use the persistence integration setup like the other services.
acceptance_criteria: 5 wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes (persisted); integration test covers lock, persistence of the counter and events, reset on success
close_reason: Failed logins now commit (own transaction, row locked FOR UPDATE): counter, login.failed and account.locked persist, 5 wrong passwords lock for 15 min; locked account returns 403 identity_account_locked; integration tests

title: Manual migrations: separate migrations image, no PreSync hooks
description: Service images ship the migrate CLI and SQL (0492edd) and infra runs them automatically as PreSync hooks (ae412b5). Decision: migrations are run by hand in every environment, and service images should not carry the migration tool. Build a separate ghcr.io/rasparac/<svc>-migrations image per service with a schema (same tag as the service), revert the service Dockerfile, remove the hooks, add task migrate -- <env> <service> [tag] in rekreativko-infra (one-off Job against the current kubectl context, with confirmation). CI and release PRs warn when a change includes new migrations.
close_reason: Service images back to the service only; ghcr.io/rasparac/<svc>-migrations built per service with the same tag (build/migrations.Dockerfile); PreSync hooks removed (infra 4c76529); task migrate runs migrations by hand; dev deploy warns and release PRs flag migration changes.

title: k8s has no working database migration step
description: docker-compose applies every service's migrations with a migrate container (one x-migrations-table per service), but k8s has nothing equivalent: services don't migrate on startup, and rekreativko-infra's task k8s-migrate uses an undefined {{.MIGRATIONS_DIR}}, a broken host ($localhost) and no per-service migrations table. So the in-cluster postgres only has schema that was applied by hand, and notifications/location have none; notifications' new JetStream consumers (DeliverAllPolicy) would replay the stream backlog into a DB without tables and DLQ it. /health doesn't touch the DB, so pods look healthy. Fix: a migrate Job per service run as an ArgoCD PreSync hook before its Deployment, with the migration files baked into an image CI builds; fix or remove task k8s-migrate. Workaround today: task k8s-db-local (docker-compose DB, already migrated).
close_reason: PreSync migrate Job per service using the service image (api 0492edd ships /migrations + migrate CLI; infra ae412b5), initdb pre-creates extensions to avoid the parallel CREATE EXTENSION race, task k8s-migrate re-runs hooks. Not yet exercised on a live cluster (minikube was down).

title: Fix build_and_push workflow: manual-run skip, silent bump failure, concurrency
description: workflow_dispatch 'skip' step used exit 0 which does not skip later steps, so a manual run built and bumped all 6 services. The infra bump loop passed silently after 5 rejected pushes. Overlapping main pushes could roll infra back to an older image. Also: fail-fast cancelled sibling services, yq installed from unpinned latest, inputs.version interpolated into shell.
close_reason: Gate step filters manual runs, bump step fails after 5 rejected pushes, workflow concurrency, fail-fast off, preinstalled yq, version passed via env

title: Verification code and email/phone leak into Jaeger traces
description:
shared/notification/event_handlers.go puts the plaintext verification code (attribute event.code in HandleVerificationCodeGenerated) and the recipient email/phone (event.email, event.phone in all 4 handlers) on OpenTelemetry spans. Traces are exported to Jaeger, so anyone who can read traces can read a working verification code and the user's contact details. The project already redacts secrets/PII from logs and http.target (shared/middleware/query_redact.go); spans from event handlers bypass that.

Fix: drop event.code entirely; drop event.email/event.phone (account_id + event_id are enough to correlate). Check identity's own spans/logs for the same values while at it (verification code creation, resend, verify).
acceptance_criteria: No span or log line contains a verification code, email address or phone number in identity or notifications; test asserts the span attributes of the verification handler (e.g. with tracetest.SpanRecorder)
close_reason: Removed verification code, email and phone from handler spans and identity log lines; test asserts handler span attributes; dev in-memory senders still log (dev-only, documented)

title: Make profile nickname unique
description: account_profile.profiles.nickname (CITEXT) has no unique constraint, so several users can share a nickname. Add a case-insensitive unique index (NULLs allowed - a fresh profile has none), return a 409 nickname_taken instead of a 500 on conflict, and make the seed script reject duplicate nicknames in its YAML.
close_reason: Unique (CITEXT, case-insensitive) index uq_profiles_nickname on account_profile.profiles WHERE deleted_at IS NULL in 000001; repo maps the violation to ErrNickNameAlreadyExists -> 409 nickname_exists; fixed invalid-nickname error wrapping (500 -> 422); seed script rejects duplicate nicknames. Verified via integration test and through the gateway.

title: account-profile: saving unchanged settings returns 500 (version conflict)
description: PUT /account-profile/api/v1/my/settings with values equal to the current ones returns HTTP 500. AccountProfileSettings.UpdateSettings (domain/account_settings.go:84) returns early without bumping the version when nothing changed, but AccountProfileSettingsManager.UpdateSettings (infrastructure/persistence/user_settings_repository.go) still runs UPDATE ... WHERE version = Version-1, which matches no row -> 'version conflict: expected version 1, but was 2'. Repro: run task seed:users twice (user with settings). Fix: have the domain method report whether anything changed and skip the save when not. Also: accountSettingsService.UpdateSettings (application/account_settings_service.go:113) saves with ctx instead of tCtx, so the write runs outside the read's transaction.
close_reason: UpdateSettings reports whether anything changed and the service skips the save when not (no more version-conflict 500); write now runs in the transaction (tCtx); domain + integration tests

title: Waitlist promotion lets an unapproved join request into an approval-gated session
description: AttendeeRepository.GetFirstPendingAttendee returns the oldest attendee with status 'pending' regardless of source. In an approval-gated session a join request is also status 'pending' (source 'requested'). When a confirmed attendee leaves, promoteNextPending promotes that first pending row - so an unapproved requester becomes 'promoted' (going) without any manager approving them, bypassing ApproveAttendee. Fix: promotion only considers waitlisted attendees (exclude source 'requested'); requests are decided only by Approve/Reject. Test: capacity 2 approval-gated session, two requests, approve one, that person cancels -> the other must still be pending. Found while writing tests for tf6.

title: Monthly recurrence: NextOccurrenceAfter returns the same occurrence again, so the session generator never advances
description: domain/recurrence.go nextMonthly falls back to nextValidMonth(year, int(after.Month())*r.interval, day) - month MULTIPLIED by the interval instead of month PLUS the interval. For interval 1 that is the same month, so NextOccurrenceAfter(O) returns O itself (not strictly after). SessionGeneratorService walks occurrences with currentTime = *nextOccurrence; NextOccurrenceAfter(currentTime), so for a monthly template currentTime never moves: the cron job loops creating the same session (or failing on it) until it is killed. Fix: month + interval. Tests: the next occurrence is strictly after the given time, steps by the interval, skips months without the day (31st), crosses the year, and respects endsAt. Found while writing tests for tf6.

title: Attendee list: non-managers lost the 'maybe' list (4ln over-restricted)
description: 4ln limited GET /sessions/{id}/attendees for non-managers to going/promoted. Mobile shows 'maybe' people to everyone and asks for them with status=maybe, so for non-organizers that section is now empty (status=maybe AND status IN (going,promoted) matches nothing). Maybe is not sensitive (it was public before and the app renders it for all); what must stay manager-only is pending (waitlist/join requests) and not_going. Fix: non-managers get going, promoted and maybe; status=pending/not_going still return nothing for them. Acceptance: non-manager asking status=maybe gets only the maybes (no going people, no duplicates), asking nothing gets going+promoted+maybe; pending/not_going stay hidden; docs and swagger updated.
close_reason: Non-managers get going, promoted and maybe in the attendee list (status=maybe returns exactly the maybes); pending and not_going stay manager-only

title: Team formation reset: clear teams when anyone leaves, and let the organizer delete teams
description:
Product decision from mobile manual testing 2026-10-04 (mobile tickets mobile-app-a01.21 and the reset rule). Observed: on session c588f245 everyone left except the creator and the session still has its 2 drafted teams; there is no endpoint to delete teams (only POST /teams, draft and proposal routes).

Wanted behaviour: a full RESET of team formation = the session goes back to its initial state, 'like there was never any draft':
- delete the session's teams and team_config (everyone unassigned),
- cancel a running captain draft and an open voting round (new cancel reason, e.g. roster_changed / teams_reset), proposals removed,
- clients must no longer see the old draft as the 'latest draft' (GET /sessions/{id}/draft -> 404 or a reset marker), because mobile only offers 'Propose teams' when there was no draft or the latest was cancelled; after a reset proposals must be allowed again.

Triggers:
1) Automatically whenever a confirmed attendee (going/promoted) stops holding a spot: cancels their RSVP (DELETE /rsvp), switches to maybe/not_going, or is removed by a manager. 'Always restart' — any leaver resets, not just team members. (This replaces today's AttendeeLeft behaviour of removing them from the draft pool / proposals and the leaver-only team unassign.)
2) Manually: new organizer endpoint, e.g. DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}/teams (canManageSession; 409 if session canceled/completed), same reset.

Also: emit a stream update (snapshot with no teams/draft/voting) and decide notifications (probably notify people who were on teams that teams were reset). Open question for product: should a new joiner also reset teams? (Not requested; today they stay unassigned.)
acceptance_criteria: Any confirmed attendee leaving/removed/stepping down to maybe resets teams, draft and voting to the initial state; organizer can do the same via the new endpoint; GET /draft no longer reports the old draft; stream snapshot reflects it; tests.
notes: Product decision 2026-10-04: a new joiner does NOT reset teams (they stay unassigned) - for now.
close_reason: Team formation reset: any confirmed attendee leaving (cancel RSVP, maybe/not_going, removed) or DELETE /sessions/{id}/teams deletes teams, cancels draft/vote, clears draft+vote history; teams_reset event + team_formation_reset notification; joiners do not reset

title: Add geocoding proxy/cache service for Nominatim (replace direct mobile->Nominatim calls)
description:
## Problem

The mobile app currently calls https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org directly from the client to resolve lat/long <-> City/Country. This has several downsides:

- No control over Nominatim's usage policy (max 1 req/sec, requires a valid User-Agent/Referer, no heavy uniform polling) - risk of the app's IP/traffic getting rate-limited or blocked since all requests originate from many individual mobile clients instead of one identifiable backend.
- No caching - repeated lookups for the same City/Country (or the same lat/long bucket) always hit Nominatim again, wasting quota and adding latency for users.
- No observability - we cannot trace, meter, or alert on geocoding calls the way we do for our own services (OpenTelemetry/Prometheus).
- Mobile team is coupled to a third-party API contract directly (shape of Nominatim responses leaks into the app).
- Nominatim/OSM usage policy requires attribution and a proper User-Agent identifying the application - easy to get wrong when called from many client installs, easy to enforce centrally from one backend service.

## Proposed solution

Introduce a new backend service (working name: `location` or `geocoding`) that sits between mobile and Nominatim:

```
mobile -> gateway -> location-service -> nominatim -> location-service -> mobile
```

Responsibilities:
1. Expose our own REST endpoints (via the gateway, following the existing routing/auth pattern in gateway/internal) for:
   - Reverse geocoding: lat/long -> City/Country (and any other fields the app needs).
   - (Optional/forward-looking) Forward geocoding: City/Country -> lat/long, if/when mobile needs it.
2. Proxy requests to Nominatim's API on the backend, setting a proper User-Agent per Nominatim's usage policy and enforcing our own outbound rate limiting (mirroring Nominatim's max 1 req/sec policy) so we don't get blocked.
3. Cache results in PostgreSQL (or Redis, see open questions) keyed by normalized City+Country (and/or rounded lat/long) so repeated lookups for the same location don't hit Nominatim again.
4. Follow existing service conventions from CLAUDE.md "Adding a New Service": DDD layering (domain/application/infrastructure/interfaces), own cmd entrypoint, own migration(s) for the cache table, registered in gateway router, added to docker-compose.yaml, service-specific Prometheus metrics.

## Why this matters / priority

- Direct third-party calls from a mobile client are a latent production risk: if Nominatim rate-limits or blocks our traffic (shared IP ranges, missing/invalid User-Agent, bursty usage), reverse-geocoding breaks for all users with no server-side fallback or visibility.
- This is straightforward to introduce now (before the mobile app has many more direct integration points against Nominatim) and unlocks caching, cost/latency savings, and observability.

## Scope / Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New service scaffolded following existing DDD conventions (domain/application/infrastructure/interfaces + metrics), with its own cmd entrypoint.
- [ ] Endpoint(s) for reverse geocoding (lat/long -> City/Country) exposed through the gateway, following existing auth/routing rules.
- [ ] Outbound calls to Nominatim set a compliant User-Agent and respect Nominatim's usage policy (rate limiting to <= 1 req/sec).
- [ ] Results are cached (DB table or Redis) keyed by normalized location, with a defined TTL/invalidation strategy, so repeat lookups for the same City/Country avoid a new Nominatim call.
- [ ] Service registered in docker-compose.yaml and gateway router.
- [ ] Basic Prometheus metrics for the new service (request counts/latency, cache hit/miss ratio, Nominatim call counts).
- [ ] Mobile team has a documented contract (endpoint + request/response shape) to switch to, replacing their direct Nominatim calls.

## Open questions (to resolve during design/implementation)

- Cache store: shared PostgreSQL table (consistent with "shared DB across services" pattern) vs. Redis (already used for caching elsewhere)?
- Cache key normalization strategy: exact City+Country string match vs. rounded lat/long grid buckets vs. both.
- TTL for cached entries (Nominatim data can change, e.g. new addresses) - or treat City/Country resolution as effectively immutable and cache indefinitely.
- Whether to also cover forward geocoding (City/Country -> lat/long) now or in a follow-up.
- New service name/port and whether it lives under an existing bounded context (e.g. account-profile, since it's used for user location context) or as a standalone service.
close_reason: Location service implemented (commit e233b69): reverse+forward geocoding via gateway, Nominatim UA + 1 req/s limiter, Postgres bucket cache, metrics, compose, swagger and README contract. All acceptance criteria verified in code.

title: ReconstructActivityGroup drops capacity - GetActivityGroupByID always returns nil DefaultCapacity, so group capacity is never enforced
description:
activity/internal/domain/activity_group.go's ReconstructActivityGroup(id, creatorID, title, description, activityType, difficultyLevel, visibility, status, location, timezone, capacity, createdAt, updatedAt, cancelledAt, deletedAt) *ActivityGroup accepts a capacity *Capacity parameter but never assigns it in the returned &ActivityGroup{...} struct literal - the capacity field is simply omitted, so it's left at its zero value (nil) regardless of what's passed in.

activity_group_repo.go's GetActivityGroupByID (and mapActivityGroupModelToDomain) correctly scans default_capacity from the DB and constructs a non-nil *domain.Capacity when the column is non-NULL, then passes it into ReconstructActivityGroup - but that value is silently discarded. Confirmed via a debug test: creating an ActivityGroup with capacity=1 and immediately calling GetActivityGroupByID on it returns group.DefaultCapacity() == nil.

Impact: every capacity check in member_service.go (RequestToJoin's up-front check and ApproveMember's re-check, both guarded by 'if capacity := group.DefaultCapacity(); capacity != nil') is unconditionally skipped for ANY activity group loaded from the database, since GetActivityGroupByID is the only way application code loads a persisted group. This means activity group capacity limits have never been enforced at runtime - not a concurrency bug, a total no-op, independent of the TOCTOU race fixed for group capacity in rekreativko-api-b8q (which cannot even be verified/exercised until this is fixed, since the capacity-check block itself never runs).

Fix: add capacity: capacity, to the &ActivityGroup{...} struct literal in ReconstructActivityGroup.
close_reason: ReconstructActivityGroup was silently dropping its capacity parameter instead of assigning it to the struct, so GetActivityGroupByID always returned nil DefaultCapacity and group capacity was never enforced regardless of concurrency. Fixed by assigning capacity: capacity in the struct literal; verified via a debug test that round-trips a group through create+load.

title: CreateRSVP capacity downgrade is dead code for non-approval 'going' RSVPs
description: In activity/internal/application/attendee_service.go's CreateRSVP, the non-approval 'going' branch calls domain.NewRSVPManualAttendee(session, groupID, userID, status) which sets a.status = status (i.e. AttendeeStatusGoing) immediately, then calls attendee.UpdateRSVP(status, session, confirmedCount) to apply the capacity-aware downgrade-to-pending logic. But domain.Attendee.UpdateRSVP's very first line is 'if newStatus == a.status { return nil // no change }' - since a.status is already Going (set by NewRSVPManualAttendee above) and newStatus is also Going, this check is always true, so UpdateRSVP returns immediately without ever running the hasCapacity check. Net effect: a brand-new RSVP to a non-approval-gated session for status='going' is ALWAYS created as 'going', regardless of session capacity - overbooking every full session's non-approval-gated 'going' RSVP path, independent of any concurrency (this is a sequential logic bug, not the TOCTOU race fixed in rekreativko-api-b48, though it compounds it). The capacity check only actually works today via UpdateRSVP (an existing attendee changing status to going, where oldStatus != Going) and via CreateRSVP's approval-gated branch (a separate HasCapacity check before creating a pending join request). Fix: in CreateRSVP's non-approval branch, create the attendee with an initial status of Pending (or via a status-less constructor) and then call UpdateRSVP(status, session, confirmedCount) to let it decide the real starting status, OR check capacity before calling NewRSVPManualAttendee and pass in AttendeeStatusPending directly when the session is full.
close_reason: Made NewRSVPManualAttendee check capacity itself for status=Going (downgrading to Pending + emitting AutoPendingEvent when full) instead of relying on a follow-up UpdateRSVP call that was always a no-op since newStatus already equaled the just-constructed status. Verified with unit tests that fail without the fix.

title: Gateway API key secret committed in observability/prometheus.yml
description: The real GATEWAY_API_KEY value used to protect service-to-service auth (shared/middleware/gateway_key.go CheckGatewayKey) and the gateway /metrics endpoint (shared/middleware/metrics_auth.go RequireMetricsToken) is hardcoded in plaintext at observability/prometheus.yml:34 (credentials: "468019b5-a863-4e49-b8d8-2c420079ac7b"). This value is identical to GATEWAY_API_KEY / GATEWAY_API_KEYS in the gitignored .env file (.env:28-29), confirming it is the live secret, not a placeholder. The file's own comment (observability/prometheus.yml:26-29) explicitly warns 'in production this file must not be checked in with a real secret inlined - inject it via templating or a secret-mounted config,' but the real secret was committed anyway in commit 36cb6607. Anyone with read access to the git history/repo now has the key that authenticates as the gateway to every backend service (identity, account-profile, activity, notifications) and can also scrape the gateway's own /metrics. Fix: rotate GATEWAY_API_KEY/GATEWAY_API_KEYS immediately, remove the literal value from prometheus.yml (use envsubst/templating at container start, or a Prometheus secret file via file_sd/external secret mount), and scrub the value from git history if feasible.
close_reason: Removed hardcoded GATEWAY_API_KEY from observability/prometheus.yml; switched to credentials_file backed by a Docker Compose secret, rotated the key in .env

title: Mising visibility paramater in CresteSessionRequest
description: Mobile team currently sends two requests to when creating new Sessions. One to create and other to update visibility. We MUST give them option to send visibility in one request and do it in one request. Check if same must be done for update session
close_reason: Added visibility to CreateSessionRequest/UpdateSessionRequest (now required on both), wired through to domain SetVisibility/NewSession, and removed the standalone-must-be-public restriction so standalone sessions can be public or private.

title: identity: login/resend by email or phone can pick a deleted account after the address is re-registered
description: accounts_email_uq_idx / accounts_phonenumber_uq_idx are unique only WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, so after DELETE /me the same email/phone can register again. AccountManager.GetBy (identity/internal/infrastructure/persistence/account_repository.go) filters by email/phone without deleted_at IS NULL and uses QueryRow, which returns an arbitrary first row when two match. Login and resend-verification-code can therefore load the deleted account and fail with ErrAccountDeleted (or resend to it). Since dh7.1 the window is ACCOUNT_ERASURE_GRACE (30d) - the erase job NULLs email/phone afterwards; before it was forever. Fix: lookups by email/phone exclude deleted accounts (deleted_at IS NULL), lookups by id keep returning them. Add an integration test: register, delete, register again with the same email, login succeeds as the new account.

title: Purge dead-lettered outbox rows after a retention window
description: shared/events/outbox_purger.go only deletes published rows (DeletePublishedEvents). Rows with failed_at set (dead-lettered) are never purged, and identity payloads carry email, phone and verification codes (identity/internal/domain/account_events.go, verification_code_events.go), so personal data can stay there indefinitely, even after erasure. Purge failed rows older than a configurable window (e.g. 14d, matching the NATS DLQ dlqMaxAge) and count them in metrics.
close_reason: Outbox purger deletes dead-lettered rows older than OUTBOX_DEAD_LETTER_RETENTION (14d), counted under events_outbox_purged_total{kind=dead_lettered}

title: activity: deactivate on identity.account.deleted, erase on identity.account.erased
description: On identity.account.deleted: leave upcoming sessions (promote waitlist as usual), cancel pending group/session invites and invite links they created, leave groups, apply the ownership decision (sibling decision ticket). On identity.account.erased: soft-delete/remove remaining membership and attendee rows that are not needed for others' history; keep account_id references in historical rows (attendance, draft picks, votes) - clients render them as 'Deleted user'. Insert activity.erased_account and raise activity.account.erased in the same tx. Commands from an erased account_id are rejected (check erased_account). Idempotent handlers, integration tests.
notes: Erasure confirmation (from dh7.1): identity already subscribes to `activity.account.erased` (it is in the default ACCOUNT_ERASURE_CONTEXTS). After erasing this context's data on identity.account.erased, raise `activity.account.erased` through the outbox in the same transaction, payload {"event_id", "account_id"} (account_id only, no personal data). Until this ships, identity counts every erasure as incomplete for activity after ACCOUNT_ERASURE_INCOMPLETE_AFTER (7d) and AccountErasureIncomplete fires.

title: notifications: stop delivery and delete feed on account deletion/erasure
description: On identity.account.deleted: stop email/SMS delivery and feed creation for the account. On identity.account.erased: DELETE notifications.notification WHERE recipient_account_id = $1, insert notifications.erased_account, raise notifications.account.erased in the same tx. Feed/delivery handlers must skip any event whose recipient is in erased_account, so a late activity event cannot re-create rows. Rows that only reference the account as actor in data jsonb hold just the UUID and may stay.
notes: Erasure confirmation (from dh7.1): identity already subscribes to `notifications.account.erased` (it is in the default ACCOUNT_ERASURE_CONTEXTS). After erasing this context's data on identity.account.erased, raise `notifications.account.erased` through the outbox in the same transaction, payload {"event_id", "account_id"} (account_id only, no personal data). Until this ships, identity counts every erasure as incomplete for notifications after ACCOUNT_ERASURE_INCOMPLETE_AFTER (7d) and AccountErasureIncomplete fires.
close_reason: notifications stops delivery and feed creation on identity.account.deleted; on identity.account.erased deletes the feed, records erased_account and confirms with notifications.account.erased via a new outbox; unit + integration tests

title: Decide: what happens to groups, templates and sessions created by an erased account
description: activity.activity_group.creator_id, session_template.created_by_id and session.created_by_id are NOT NULL. When the creator erases their account: hand ownership to the longest-standing admin, else cancel/delete the group and its future sessions? Standalone sessions they created? Also decide whether free text they authored (group title/description, session note, location_street) is kept, since it may contain personal data. Record the decision in .claude/docs/activity.md.

title: identity: grace period, erase cron, identity.account.erased and erasure tracking
description: Per the epic design. Schema (edit identity 000001): accounts.erase_after timestamptz, accounts.erased_at timestamptz; table identity.account_erasure(account_id, context, completed_at, PK(account_id, context)). Domain: Account.Erase() NULLs email/phone, sets an unusable password sentinel (column is NOT NULL), sets erased_at, raises AccountErasedEvent with account_id only. DeleteAccount sets erase_after = now + ACCOUNT_ERASURE_GRACE (envconfig, default 30d, 0 = erase on next cron run). Cron step: batch accounts with erase_after < now AND erased_at IS NULL, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, erase + delete verification_codes and refresh_tokens in one tx. Subscribe to <context>.account.erased acks and fill account_erasure; expected contexts from config; Prometheus gauge/alert for erasures not completed after N days. Tests: domain unit tests + repository integration test.
close_reason: Deleted accounts are erased after ACCOUNT_ERASURE_GRACE by a batched SKIP LOCKED job raising identity.account.erased; <context>.account.erased confirmations tracked in identity.account_erasure with an incomplete-erasure gauge and alert

title: GDPR account erasure: every bounded context erases its own data
description: DELETE /api/v1/me (identity/internal/application/service.go:147) only soft-deletes: email, phone_number and password stay in identity.accounts forever, and identity.account.deleted is published but has no consumer, so profile (full_name, date_of_birth, coordinates, bio, picture), activity and notifications data is never erased. Hashing email/nickname/coords is pseudonymisation (still personal data, GDPR Recital 26) and does not satisfy Art. 17 - values must be NULLed or rows deleted. The random account_id UUID may stay as a reference ('Deleted user') once nothing identifying is linked to it. Art. 12(3): complete within one month.
design:
Grace period lives ONLY in identity; every other context deletes immediately on an event (no per-service mark-for-deletion: that would duplicate scheduling and force every query to hide 'marked' rows).
1. DELETE /me: identity sets status=deleted, deleted_at, erase_after = now + ACCOUNT_ERASURE_GRACE (config, 0 allowed), revokes tokens, raises identity.account.deleted (existing). Consumers only deactivate: activity leaves upcoming sessions/cancels pending invites, notifications stops delivery.
2. Identity cron: accounts with erase_after < now AND erased_at IS NULL -> NULL email/phone, unusable password sentinel, delete verification_codes + refresh_tokens, set erased_at, raise identity.account.erased {account_id only} in the same tx (outbox).
3. Each context consumes identity.account.erased and hard-deletes / NULLs its own rows in one tx, explicit child-first DELETEs (no ON DELETE CASCADE - same locks, but deletion stays visible in the repo). Handlers idempotent (at-least-once delivery).
4. Tracking: each context writes <schema>.erased_account(account_id PK, erased_at) in the same tx. Uses: (a) idempotency, (b) drop late events that would re-create data for an erased account (e.g. a notification for a session), (c) replay erasure after a backup restore. Each context then raises <context>.account.erased; identity records it in identity.account_erasure(account_id, context, completed_at) against a configured list of contexts, and a metric/alert fires for erasures incomplete after N days (Art. 5(2) accountability).
Schema changes go into the existing 000001_* migrations (project not in production).
acceptance_criteria: After DELETE /me and the grace period, no table in any schema holds the account's email, phone, password, name, date of birth, location, bio, picture or notifications; the profile picture file is gone; identity.account_erasure shows every context completed; an integration test covers the full flow.

title: CI: stop dev image bumps racing each other (one matrix job always fails)
description: Build & Deploy to Dev ran bump-infra-image.sh from each of the 8 matrix jobs, all pushing to infra main at once; with 5 attempts and 1-5s jitter one job always ran out of attempts (identity failed 5 times in a row). Fix: matrix jobs only build and upload a built-<service> artifact with the tag; a single deploy-dev job (needs build-and-push, if !cancelled) downloads them and bumps the services one after another. A failed build uploads nothing so it is never bumped. The script now removes a leftover infra-repo clone dir so it can run repeatedly.
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive merges to main: no red deploy step; infra main gets one bump commit per built service; a failed build leaves only that service red and does not block the others' bump

title: Identity: feature flag to skip account verification at registration
description:
Registration creates a pending account that can only log in after verify-account with an emailed code. For the first release, drop-off at that step costs users, and outside dev mode the notifications service cannot start (no real SMTP sender), so verification cannot work in a deployed environment yet.

Add ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED (default true). When false, Register creates the account active (no verification code), still raising registered/activated/verified events so account-profile creates the profile; the verified event is marked unconfirmed so notifications sends no welcome email to an unproven address. Client then calls login as usual. Turning the flag back on only affects new sign-ups.

Follow-up (separate ticket): soft verification - separate email_verified field, required only for sensitive actions (password reset, ...). Accounts created while the flag was off are unverified.
acceptance_criteria: Flag off: register returns an active account, login works immediately, profile is created, no welcome email, no verification code row; flag on: behavior unchanged; tests for both; READMEs/CLAUDE.md describe the flag
close_reason: ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED flag (default true); off activates the account at registration, no code, unconfirmed verified event so no welcome email; tests, docs, dev overlay off

title: GET /profiles?limit=N skips the missing-filter guard and lists every profile
description:
Found in o34. account-profile/internal/interfaces/http/mapper/query_params.go sets hasFilter = true when a limit query param is present, so GET /profiles?limit=100000 passes the ErrMissingAccountProfilesFilter check and returns every profile (full_name, date_of_birth, location, bio, activity interests) to any logged-in user. A limit is not a filter. Verified by a throwaway test: limit=100000 and limit=0 parse without error and with no other filter.

Fix: do not count limit/page_token/sort as filters; only account_id, nickname, city, country, date-of-birth bounds. Separately consider whether city/country/age searches should be open to every user at all (privacy settings are not enforced either, see account-profile README). Test: ?limit=... alone is rejected with 400.
acceptance_criteria: limit alone returns 400 missing filter; test; decision recorded on whether filter searches stay open
notes: WIDER THAN LIMIT: query_params.go also sets hasFilter for include_deleted, sort_by and sort_order, so GET /profiles?sort_by=nickname (or include_deleted=false) alone also passes the guard and lists everyone. Only selection criteria are filters: account_id, nickname, dob_gt, dob_lt, country, city. Audit (o34 follow-up): the mobile app uses /profiles only by account_id (repeated, rosters and one id) and by one nickname; the city/country/dob/sort/include_deleted filters are used by no client (checked mobile-app, scripts/seed-users, backend callers: none besides the gateway proxy).
close_reason: GET /profiles: only account_id, nickname, dob_gt/lt, country, city count as filters (limit, sort_by, sort_order, include_deleted no longer bypass the guard); tests

title: GET /profiles roster lookup is truncated to 20: profiles of a roster over 20 are missing
description:
Found in o34. The app resolves a whole roster with GET /profiles?account_id=a&account_id=b... in one call (shared/api/accountProfileClient.ts) and reads only items, but the endpoint applies the default limit 20. Verified with an integration test: 25 account_ids -> 20 profiles + next_page_token (limit=0 or 100000 -> 25). Attendees can be 200 and group members are unlimited, so names/avatars of everyone after the 20th are missing.

Fix: a lookup by account_id returns every requested profile and is not paginated: cap the number of ids (e.g. 200, 400 above it) and ignore limit in that mode; keep pagination for filter searches. Mobile: chunk by the cap if a roster can exceed it. Test: 25 ids -> 25 profiles, 201 ids -> 400.
acceptance_criteria: 25+ ids return all profiles in one response; more than the cap is a 400; integration test; mobile handover noted
notes: MOBILE HANDOVER: GET /profiles with account_id (and/or nickname) now returns every match in one response, not a page of 20: rosters over 20 now resolve fully. At most 100 account_id + nickname values per request: more returns 400 bad_request. getDisplayNames / fetchProfilesByAccountIds must send ids in chunks of 100 (attendee rosters reach 200, group members are unbounded). limit/page_token are ignored for lookups. Sending no selecting filter (e.g. only limit or sort_by) now returns 400, the app never does.
close_reason: GET /profiles lookup by account_id/nickname returns every match in one response (not paged), max 100 values then 400; integration test fails before (20 of 25), mapper tests, README, mobile handover

title: List endpoints accept any limit: no upper bound, and limit=0 returns the whole table
description:
Found in o34. api.ParsePageParams (shared/api/page.go) only rejects negative limits. Verified: limit=100000 is accepted by /profiles and /activity-groups, and limit=0 means 'no LIMIT' in the activity repositories (they all do 'if filter.Limit > 0'), so ?limit=0 on /activity-groups, /activity-groups/discover, /sessions, /sessions/discover, members and templates returns the entire table. Any authenticated caller can dump or stress it.

Fix: clamp limit in one place (ParsePageParams or a MaxLimit in the services), e.g. default 20, max 100; treat 0 as the default; keep the repo-level 'Limit > 0' only for internal callers. Tests: limit 0 / huge / negative on each list mapper.
acceptance_criteria: limit has a server-side maximum and 0 no longer means unlimited, on every paginated endpoint; tests; swagger/README note of the max
notes: MOBILE HANDOVER: limit on paginated lists is now at most 100 (a larger value is cut to 100, the response's limit shows the size used); limit=0 means the default 20, not everything. The app sends 10, 20 and 50, so nothing changes for it. A page smaller than asked for is not the end of the list: only a missing next_page_token is.
close_reason: ParsePageParams caps limit at 100 and treats 0 as the default (it reached the repositories as no LIMIT); all list endpoints go through it; unit tests (fail on the old parser), swagger and README

title: Gateway rate limiting: per-account keys, stricter auth endpoints, Retry-After, exempt streams
description:
Design follow-up from the 1nj investigation. Today: one in-memory fixed-window limiter, 60 req/min per client key, same bucket for login, page loads, polling and SSE connects; a burst early in the window blocks the key for the rest of the minute; 429 carries no Retry-After.
- Authenticated requests: key by account id (the JWT subject, available after RequireAuth) so six users behind one NAT do not share 60/min; unauthenticated ones by client IP (see the GetIP ticket).
- Separate, stricter limits for login / register / verify-account / resend (credential stuffing, SMS/email cost); a looser overall limit for the rest.
- Do not count or cheapen: CORS preflight (already before the limiter), health, long-lived SSE connects (one per connect, not per event).
- Token bucket (or sliding window) instead of a fixed window so a burst is smoothed instead of locking the user out for the minute.
- Always send Retry-After (seconds to the next token) on 429.
- Single gateway instance today: in-memory is fine; note Redis-backed (Redis already runs) if it scales to several instances.
- Pick the numbers from measured use: a Home load is ~6 requests, a session page ~8, idle polling ~4/min, 3-5s fallback polling 12-36/min per open screen.
acceptance_criteria: Limits keyed per account/IP as above; auth endpoints limited separately; Retry-After on 429; tests; README/gateway docs updated; mobile handover noted
notes: MOBILE HANDOVER: a 429 now always carries Retry-After (whole seconds). Do not retry a 429 immediately (queryClient retry: 2 triples the load): wait Retry-After once, then give up. Logged-in requests are limited per account (burst 120, 90/min), not per IP. login is 10/min per IP, register/verify-account/resend-verification-code 5/min per IP, refresh-token 60/min per IP. Gateway env: RATE_LIMIT_<IP|ACCOUNT|ANONYMOUS|LOGIN|SENSITIVE>_BURST / _PER_MINUTE; REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE is removed.
close_reason: Token-bucket limiter: per-IP backstop before auth, per-account limit after auth, stricter login/register/verify/resend limits per IP, Retry-After on 429; tests, real-binary probe and gateway README

title: Gateway client IP: everyone shares one rate-limit bucket without proxy headers, and forwarded headers can be spoofed
description:
shared/middleware/client_info.go GetIP (used by the rate limiter, the access log and ClientInfo) has two problems, both confirmed (see 1nj notes):
1. No RemoteAddr fallback. Despite the comment, when none of CF-Connecting-IP / True-Client-IP / X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP / Forwarded is set, GetIP returns "". Every request then shares the rate-limiter key "" (one 60/min bucket for ALL clients) and logs have ip_address="". All 778 requests in the local gateway log have ip_address="". Probe: 2 clients without proxy headers, 100 requests -> 60 ok / 40 limited.
2. Forwarded headers are trusted unconditionally and in this order: CF-Connecting-IP first. One client rotating X-Forwarded-For passes 1000/1000 requests; the limiter and the logged/event IP are spoofable. In k8s, nginx ingress overwrites X-Forwarded-For by default but passes unknown headers like CF-Connecting-IP / True-Client-IP through from the client, which GetIP prefers, so it is spoofable there too.

Fix: fall back to the connection's RemoteAddr (host part); trust forwarded headers only when the direct peer is in a configured trusted-proxy list (e.g. TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS; the ingress / pod network), and then use only one agreed header (X-Forwarded-For, rightmost untrusted hop, or X-Real-IP); drop the Cloudflare headers unless Cloudflare is really in front. Keep the access log IP and the account's login-attempt IP consistent (Account.RecordFailedLoginAttempt stores it too).

Tests: GetIP table test (no header -> RemoteAddr; header from untrusted peer ignored; from trusted proxy used; IPv6; port stripped); limiter test with two RemoteAddrs gets two buckets.
acceptance_criteria: GetIP never returns empty for a real connection; forwarded headers only honoured from trusted proxies; table tests; README/CLAUDE.md note on TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS
close_reason: Gateway resolves client IP only from trusted proxies (TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS), rightmost-untrusted X-Forwarded-For hop, spoofed headers ignored, backends receive resolved IP; tests and README added

title: Identity: rethink the failed-login lock policy now that lockout works (year-long lock, never-decaying counter)
description:
With hsa fixed, the lock policy in Account.RecordFailedLoginAttempt is live for the first time and has problems:
- 10 failures lock the account for 365 days with no unlock path (Account.Unlock is not reachable from any route), so anyone who knows an email/phone can lock that person out for a year with 10 wrong guesses (targeted lockout DoS).
- failedLoginAttempts is not reset when a lock expires, only by a successful login. So a user who fails 5 times, waits out the 15 minutes and then fails once more is immediately locked again, and 10 failures spread over any period reach the year-long lock.
- The user gets no notice that their account was locked (no email/SMS; the lockout alert was dropped in yn0). Whether to send one is open.
Decide: decay/reset the counter when the lock expires or after a quiet period; replace the year-long lock with progressive back-off (15m, 1h, 24h) or an unlock-by-email flow; whether to alert the user. Also consider per-IP limits at the gateway (see 1nj, X-Forwarded-For).
acceptance_criteria: No lock is longer than 24h; back-off tiers 15m/1h/24h with tests (domain + Service.Login integration); identity/README.md updated
notes: Decision: tiered back-off, no permanent lock. 5th consecutive failure -> 15 min, 10th -> 1 h, 15th and later -> 24 h (cap); the count is kept when a lock expires (so the next wrong password re-locks for the tier of the new count) and cleared only by a successful login; counting stops at 15. Schema unchanged. Not done (separate decisions): lockout email/SMS to the user (dropped in yn0), an unlock-by-email flow, per-IP limits at the gateway (see 1nj). Residual: someone who knows an email can still keep that account locked for up to 24 h by guessing.
close_reason: Tiered lock back-off 15m/1h/24h, never permanent; count stops at 15, cleared by successful login; domain + integration tests

title: k8s app services ignore the DB credentials in app-secrets
description: Services read POSTGRES_USER / POSTGRES_PASSWORD (shared/config), but rekreativko-infra's app-secrets provides DATABASE_USERNAME / DATABASE_PASSWORD (only the postgres StatefulSet maps them). The apps therefore connect with the code defaults postgres/postgres, which only works because the dev secret happens to use the same values. Any other password (or a managed prod DB) would break auth. Fix: map the secret keys to POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_PASSWORD in the app deployments (env valueFrom) or rename the secret keys and reseal; don't rely on code defaults for credentials.
close_reason: App containers map app-secrets DATABASE_USERNAME/PASSWORD to POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD via env.valueFrom (infra ae412b5).

title: Sessions: one definition of 'ended', upcoming/past list filter, automatic completion
description:
Past sessions leak into lists and are never marked completed.

Findings:
1. GET /sessions (group sessions, My Activities) has no time filter by default and sorts start_time ASC, so past sessions are included and, with history, fill the first page (mobile reads one page of 50-100) and push upcoming ones out. Mobile hides canceled but not ended sessions there; the group detail screen filters nothing.
2. GET /sessions/discover filters status='scheduled' AND (end_time IS NULL OR end_time > now()) (session_repo.go DiscoverSessions). end_time is optional, so a session without one stays in discover forever. A started-but-not-ended session is also shown (maybe intended).
3. Session.ExpireSchedule / SessionService.ExpireCompletedSessions (FindSessionsPastEndTime: status IN scheduled,started AND end_time < now()) only runs in activity-cron, which compose does not schedule (manual: docker compose run --rm activity-cron), and it skips sessions without end_time. So past sessions stay 'scheduled'. Mobile's MyActivitiesScreen comment says nothing server-side ever flips a session to completed; it filters with hasEnded(end_time) client-side.

Proposal:
- Define one rule for 'ended': end_time if set, else start_time + a configurable default duration (e.g. 3h). Use it in discover, the list filter and the expiry job (FindSessionsPastEndTime).
- GET /sessions: add when=upcoming|past. Default upcoming sorted soonest first; past sorted most recent first (history). Breaking default change, needs a mobile handover.
- Run the expiry automatically (in-process ticker in the activity service, like the notifications retention sweep uvh; idempotent so several instances are fine) instead of relying on a manual cron.
- Decide whether started-but-not-ended sessions count as upcoming.
acceptance_criteria: Ended rule defined once and used by discover, list filter and expiry; GET /sessions when=upcoming|past; expiry runs without manual cron; integration tests; mobile handover in ticket notes
notes:
Decisions: ended = end_time, else start_time + 3h (domain.DefaultSessionDuration, constant not config); a started-but-not-ended session counts as upcoming; canceled sessions follow the same time rule (no status special-casing). when=upcoming|past|all, default upcoming; past sorts newest first. Expiry runs in the API service every ACTIVITY_SESSION_EXPIRY_INTERVAL (5m, 0 disables), reloading each session under its lock so several instances are safe; activity-cron still does it too. Side effect: a session started manually without an end_time is auto-completed 3h after its start_time.

Mobile handover:
- GET /sessions now returns only upcoming sessions by default (end not passed; running ones included), soonest first. Pass when=past for history (newest first, same page_token paging) or when=all for the old unfiltered list. Invalid value -> 422 invalid_session_timeframe.
- GET /sessions/discover now also drops sessions without end_time once start+3h has passed.
- Sessions now actually become status=completed after they end (activity.session.expired event), also those without end_time.
- Client: hasEnded(end_time) in MyActivitiesScreen/HomeScreen can stay as a guard for a few minutes of expiry lag but is no longer needed for correctness; hasEnded ignores sessions without end_time, which the server now handles. Group detail's session list no longer gets history mixed in; a 'Past sessions' section can call when=past.
close_reason: One 'ended' rule (end_time or start+3h) used by discover, GET /sessions when=upcoming|past|all, and expiry; expiry now runs in the API service on a ticker (multi-instance safe); tests + README

title: Invites: GET /invites and /session-invites as one unpaginated list
description:
Same as 89d/uvh. Mobile's invites badge is items.length of GET /invites and /session-invites with limit 50 (HomeScreen InvitesButton), and InvitesScreen pages session invites. Both lists are bounded by nature: one pending invite per group/session per user (unique constraints) and invites expire after 7 days.

- Both return api.List {items}, newest first, capped at 100 (MaxListedInvites, warn when hit). limit/page_token ignored; limit/next_page_token dropped from the response.
- Fix: GET /invites lists expired-but-unswept group invites (no expires_at > NOW() filter, unlike session invites; the expiry cron runs only on demand), so they inflate the badge and fail on accept. Add the filter.
- No mobile changes; hand over the contract change.
acceptance_criteria: Both endpoints unpaginated and capped; expired group invites not listed; tests pass
notes:
Mobile handover - GET /invites and GET /session-invites:
- Response is now {items} (api.List). limit and next_page_token are gone; limit/page_token query params are ignored.
- items: newest first, pending and unexpired only, at most 100. items.length is the exact badge count (HomeScreen InvitesButton already does this).
- GET /invites no longer returns expired group invites that the expiry job hasn't swept yet - they used to inflate the badge and fail with invite_expired on accept.
- Client: drop limit/page_token from listInvites/listSessionInvites, drop next_page_token/limit from InviteListResponse/SessionInviteListResponse; InvitesScreen's session-invites useInfiniteQuery + LoadMoreButton can become a plain useQuery (one key for list and badge).

title: Notifications: one unpaginated list + retention cleanup
description:
Same idea as 89d (attendees) for GET /notifications, but the feed has no natural bound: nothing ever deletes a notification. Mobile already reads only one page (50 on NotificationsScreen, 20 on Home) and never pages.

Backend:
- GET /notifications returns {items, unread_count}, newest first, capped at 100 (MaxListedNotifications). limit/page_token are no longer read; next_page_token and limit are dropped from the response. unread_only stays.
- Retention: notifications deletes read notifications older than 30 days and every notification older than 90 days, from an in-process ticker (hourly). Config: NOTIFICATIONS_RETENTION_READ, NOTIFICATIONS_RETENTION_ALL, NOTIFICATIONS_RETENTION_INTERVAL. The DELETE is idempotent, so several instances running it is harmless. Index on created_at for the sweep.
- No mobile changes; hand over the contract change once done.
acceptance_criteria: List is one capped response with unread_count; retention sweep deletes per the rules (integration-tested); README updated; tests pass
notes:
Mobile handover - GET /notifications:
- Response is now {items, unread_count}. limit and next_page_token are gone; limit/page_token query params are ignored. unread_only still works.
- items: newest first, at most 100. unread_count still counts all unread, so it can exceed items.length when there are >100 unread.
- Read notifications disappear 30 days after creation, all notifications after 90 days.
- Client: drop limit/page_token from the call and next_page_token/limit from the NotificationListResponse type (modules/activity/api/types/notification.ts); NotificationsScreen (limit 50) and Home (limit 20) can just show items.
close_reason: GET /notifications returns one list capped at 100 with unread_count; in-process retention sweep deletes read notifications >30d and all >90d (configurable); unit + integration tests

title: List session attendees: several statuses in one request, no pagination
description:
The session details page sends 4 requests to GET /sessions/{id}/attendees (status=going, promoted, maybe for managers, pending for join requests), each paginated (default limit 20); the team screens (start draft, proposal builder, proposals, teams section) send 2 each (going + promoted). Attendee lists are small (~20), so pagination only costs round trips.

## Changes (activity service)
1. status is repeatable: ?status=going&status=promoted&status=pending (same convention as attendee_status / member_status). A single status keeps working; no status = every status the caller may see.
2. Unknown status -> 400 invalid_status (today it silently returns an empty list).
3. Visibility rule unchanged: for a non-manager the requested statuses are intersected with going/promoted/maybe (pending/not_going are dropped, the rest still returned); asking for your own row (user_id = yourself) still returns it.
4. No pagination: page_token and limit are no longer read; response is {items: [...]}, ordered by created_at, id (FIFO) as today. Backward compatible for the app, which only reads items - old per-status calls keep working until the app switches.
5. Hard cap of 200 rows for all statuses (not tied to capacity: capacity only bounds going/promoted, the waitlist/maybe/not_going come on top). Log a warning when the cap is hit.
6. Swagger, activity README, and the API notes for the mobile team updated.

The repository already filters by a list of statuses (AttendeeFilter.Statuses, status = ANY(...)); the change is mostly in mapper.QueryToListRSVPsParams, ListRSVPsParams and AttendeeService.ListRSVPs.

## Out of scope
Mobile app changes - hand over the new contract to the mobile team when done (one request per page: going+promoted+maybe, plus pending for managers; split rows by status/source client-side; one react-query key per session).
acceptance_criteria: One request returns several statuses; single-status requests unchanged; invalid status is 400; non-managers never get pending/not_going rows; response has no next_page_token and ignores limit/page_token; at most 200 rows with a warning log when capped; unit tests (parsing, validation, intersection) and an integration test for a multi-status request; swagger + README updated; mobile handover notes written
notes:
Mobile handover (2026-10-15):
- GET /activity/api/v1/sessions/{id}/attendees takes status repeatedly: ?status=going&status=promoted&status=maybe&status=pending. No status = every status you may see.
- Response is {items: [...]} only - no limit, no next_page_token; limit/page_token are ignored. Oldest first, at most 200 rows.
- Non-managers: pending/not_going are silently dropped from the request, the rest is returned (no error). Own row via user_id=<me> still returns any status.
- Unknown status: 422 invalid_attendee_status.
- Session details page: replace the 4 calls (going, promoted, maybe, pending) with one: status=going&status=promoted, plus maybe and pending when canManage; split rows client-side by status and, for pending, by source (requested = join request, auto_pending = waitlist).
- Team screens (StartDraft, ProposalBuilder, Proposals, TeamsSection): one call with status=going&status=promoted instead of two.
- react-query: one key per session+status set, e.g. ["session-attendees", id, statuses]; existing invalidations on ["session-attendees", id] still match.
- Backward compatible: the current per-status calls keep working, so the app can switch whenever.
close_reason: status is repeatable, list is one unpaginated {items} response capped at 200 (warning when hit), unknown status 422, non-managers' restricted statuses dropped; unit + integration tests, swagger, README; mobile handover in notes

title: Debug logs to trace a domain event end to end (outbox -> NATS -> notifications / SSE)
description:
Make one domain event traceable through every hop by filtering logs on event_id, with debug lines at each hop:
1. stored in the outbox (shared/domainevent InsertEvents) - links the HTTP request_id to the event_id
2. published by the outbox publisher (exists; move event_id into ctx)
3. received by each JetStream consumer and by broadcast subscriptions (shared/events nats_broker) - put event_id into ctx so every downstream line carries it
4. notifications: notification created / duplicate, with type and recipient
5. activity live hub: no viewers on this instance / delivered to N viewers (queued, stale, withheld, slow-consumer disconnect) / viewer removed / session gone
6. SSE stream: update written to a client (session, event, version, account)

Gotcha: the logger appends event_id from ctx on every line, so passing "event_id" explicitly as a key produces a duplicate JSON key (empty one last). Always set it via api.WithEventID.
close_reason: Debug line with event_id at every hop (outbox insert, publish, consume/broadcast receive, notification create, live hub deliver, SSE send); logger lets an explicit key win over the ctx value (was emitting duplicate event_id keys); how-to in CLAUDE.md Observability

title: Investigate frequent 429 Too Many Requests from the gateway
description:
Clients (web app, and especially multi-user testing with scripts/open-browsers) hit 429 too_many_requests often. Investigate first; decide the fix after.

## How rate limiting works today
- One limiter, only in the gateway (gateway/cmd/api/main.go, middleware chain): shared/middleware/rate_limit.go.
- Fixed 1-minute window, in memory, per client IP, REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE default 60 (shared/config RateLimiterConfig). The same limit applies to every endpoint - login, a session page load, polling and SSE connects all draw from one bucket.
- The key is middleware.GetIP (shared/middleware/client_info.go): CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, Forwarded, then RemoteAddr.
- CORS preflight (OPTIONS) is answered in the CORS middleware, which runs before the limiter.

## Hypotheses to check
1. The budget is too small for one user: a session details page open alone is ~8 requests (session, events stream, 3x attendees, draft, proposals, team-formation), plus notification badge polling, profile lookups for nicknames, react-query refetch on focus/reconnect. Measure requests per minute for a normal browsing session.
2. Everyone shares one IP locally: all browsers on one machine (and the Docker network hop) arrive as the same IP, so 6 test users share 60 requests/min. Same issue in production behind NAT (office, mobile carrier CGNAT) or if a proxy in front of the gateway doesn't set a forwarded header.
3. Polling / retries: check the app's refetch intervals and whether it retries 429 immediately (making it worse) instead of backing off; check SSE reconnect loops.
4. Fixed window: bursts at a window boundary allow up to 2x, but a burst early in the window blocks the user for the rest of the minute.

## Also found (security, decide whether to split into its own bug)
GetIP trusts client-supplied headers (X-Forwarded-For, True-Client-IP, CF-Connecting-IP...) unconditionally. Any client can send a random X-Forwarded-For on every request and get a fresh bucket each time, bypassing the limiter (and spoofing the IP in logs). Forwarded headers should only be trusted from known proxies.

## Things to measure
Gateway access logs (Loki) grouped by client IP and path for 429s; requests/min per page in the web app (browser network tab); the app's polling intervals and retry policy (../mobile-app, react-query config).

## Possible directions (for after the investigation)
Key authenticated requests by account ID (X-User-ID after auth) and only unauthenticated ones by IP; separate, stricter limits for login/register/verify/resend; exclude or cheapen SSE/long-lived streams; token bucket instead of fixed window; Redis-backed limiter if the gateway ever runs more than one instance; return Retry-After and make the app back off; trust forwarded headers only from configured proxies.
acceptance_criteria: Notes on this ticket with: measured requests/min for typical flows, which hypotheses hold, list of 429s by endpoint from logs; follow-up tickets filed for the agreed fixes (including the X-Forwarded-For bypass, if confirmed)
notes:
INVESTIGATION RESULT

Data: local gateway container log (2026-10-12, 778 requests, one test session). 85 x 429, all in 15:25-15:27: non-OPTIONS requests per minute 63 / 91 / 111 against a limit of 60. The burst = scripts/open-browsers logging in 14 users (14 x POST /login from Go-http-client) and each browser loading Home. 429s by path: notifications 20, group invites 17, session invites 17, groups/discover 15, my/profile 15, /me 1. First 429 at 15:25:13.

Hypotheses
1. Budget too small for one user: NO for a normal single user. A Home load is ~6 requests (me, my/profile, notifications, group invites, session invites, discover) plus idle polling of 3 queries every 45 s (~4/min). A session details page is ~8, but while its SSE stream is not live the screens poll draft + voting + team-formation every 5 s (3 x 12 = 36/min per open screen), and Draft/Proposals screens poll every 3 s (20/min each). One user on a dropped stream can reach ~60/min.
2. Shared IP: CONFIRMED, and worse than assumed. GetIP has no RemoteAddr fallback: with no forwarding header it returns "", and ALL 778 logged requests have ip_address="". So every client without a proxy header (local docker, anything not behind a header-setting proxy) shares ONE bucket of 60/min, and logs carry no IP. Probe test: 2 clients, no headers, 100 requests -> 60 ok / 40 limited. In k8s the nginx ingress sets X-Forwarded-For so clients are keyed per source IP (still shared behind NAT / CGNAT). -> ticket xb6.
3. Polling / retries: PARTLY. Polling alone is modest (see 1). But shared/api/queryClient.ts sets retry: 2 with react-query's default 1 s/2 s backoff, so every 429'd query is sent 3 times, tripling the load right when the bucket is empty; the app has no 429 / Retry-After handling at all (grep found none), and the server sends no Retry-After. SSE reconnects use exponential backoff (shared/live/backoff.ts) - fine.
4. Fixed window: CONFIRMED as a contributor (429s start mid-window and last to the window end), but secondary.

Security: X-Forwarded-For spoofing CONFIRMED by probe: one client rotating the header passed 1000/1000 requests (limit 60). CF-Connecting-IP / True-Client-IP are preferred over XFF and pass through nginx ingress untouched, so the bypass works in k8s too. -> ticket xb6 (together with the RemoteAddr fix).

Follow-ups filed: xb6 (P2 bug/security: GetIP fallback + trusted proxies), wd8 (P2 task: per-account keys, stricter auth limits, token bucket, Retry-After).

Mobile handover (their own tickets): do not retry 429 (queryClient retry: 2 should skip 429, or wait Retry-After once wd8 ships); lower Home polling or use the notification feed/SSE; stop fallback polling when the screen is not visible; for multi-user local testing (open-browsers) the cheapest immediate relief is a higher REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE in .env (e.g. 600) until xb6/wd8 land.
close_reason: Investigated: no RemoteAddr fallback so all clients without proxy headers share one bucket (confirmed in logs and by probe), XFF/CF header spoofing bypass confirmed, client retry:2 triples load on 429, fixed window secondary; follow-ups xb6 (client IP) and wd8 (limiter design)

title: Restructure notifications service: feed + delivery layers, move shared/notification in
description:
The notifications service bundles two unrelated jobs: (1) message delivery - stateless email/SMS for identity events, code in shared/notification even though only notifications imports it; (2) the in-app feed - notifications/internal, one table, GET /notifications + mark read. Decided 2026-10-14: no separate deployable (jobs are already isolated per durable NATS consumer; another container only adds config/deploy cost), instead one bounded context with two clear layers:

notifications/internal/
  domain/          Notification (feed item) + Message (recipient, channel, template, locale)
  application/     feed service; delivery service: pick channel -> render -> send
  infrastructure/  feed repo, (later device tokens); senders email/SMS/(push); templates/{en,...} via embed
  interfaces/      HTTP (feed, later device tokens); NATS: identity events -> delivery, activity events -> feed

Steps: move shared/notification into notifications/internal (domain/application/infrastructure split); move message text into templates (prepares localization rekreativko-api-nvr.4); update notifications/README.md (the 'name is a bit narrow' known issue) and root CLAUDE.md. Behavior must not change.

Gives push (rekreativko-api-79p), localized templates (nvr.4) and user preferences (email enabled, language) one obvious home. Splitting into its own service later, if delivery volume ever needs separate scaling, becomes copying the delivery layer out.
acceptance_criteria: shared/notification removed; no behavior change (existing tests pass, dev-mode verification code still logged by the in-memory sender); message text lives in templates; README and CLAUDE.md describe the two layers
close_reason: Notifications restructured into feed + delivery layers: shared/notification moved into notifications/internal (domain Message, DeliveryService, delivery senders, IdentityHandlers), message text in embedded per-locale templates; README and CLAUDE.md updated; no behavior change

Revised after investigation (the lockout alert is dropped; see rekreativko-api-hsa, P1: failed logins roll back so lockout never happens at all).

title: Investigate: which list endpoints don't need pagination
description:
Since the 2026-08-30 backend-wide pagination change (offset -> page_token, {items, limit} response), every list endpoint is paginated. For lists that are small and bounded by nature, this costs the client extra round trips and paging code without a real benefit. Example: the session details page calls GET /sessions/{id}/attendees three times (status=going|promoted|maybe), and each call is paginated even though attendees are capped by the session capacity.

Investigate first, change nothing yet. For each paginated list endpoint, record:
- Upper bound: what limits the list size (capacity, group size, expiry, nothing) and the realistic maximum.
- Client use: how the mobile app calls it (../mobile-app). Does it page through everything, read only the first page, or call it several times (e.g. once per status)?
- Recommendation: keep pagination / remove it and return the whole list / keep it but with a higher default limit / merge calls (e.g. attendees grouped by status in one response).

Endpoints to cover (GET, paginated today):
- activity: /sessions/{sessionId}/attendees, /invites, /session-invites, /activity-groups/{groupId}/members, /activity-groups/{groupId}/templates, /sessions, /sessions/discover, /activity-groups, /activity-groups/discover
- notifications: /notifications (grows without limit, so it likely stays paginated; check whether read notifications are ever purged)
- account-profile: /profiles

Things to weigh: removing pagination changes the response shape, so it is a breaking change for the mobile app and needs a coordinated release. An unbounded list without pagination needs a hard server-side cap so it can't become a DoS vector.
acceptance_criteria: A table in this ticket's notes with every paginated list endpoint: upper bound, how the client calls it, recommendation; follow-up tickets filed for each endpoint whose change is agreed
notes:
INVESTIGATION RESULT (2026-10-17, code read in rekreativko-api and ../mobile-app; the limit and roster findings verified with throwaway tests, since deleted)

ALREADY UNPAGINATED (tickets uvh, 6g1, 3do; limit/page_token ignored, service-level cap, Warn if the cap cuts the list)
- GET /notifications: cap 100, read ones purged by retention (RetentionRead/All). Mobile: one call (Home, Notifications screen).
- GET /invites, /session-invites: cap 100 each. Mobile: one call each (Home, Invites screen).
- GET /sessions/{id}/attendees: cap 200 (MaxListedAttendees). Mobile: ONE call with status list (useSessionAttendees), no longer three.

STILL PAGINATED
| Endpoint | Upper bound | Mobile use | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET /activity-groups/{id}/members | none: groups have no member cap | 2 single-page calls (status=confirmed, status=pending), default limit 20, never pages. Group with >20 confirmed members shows only the first 20; a manager sees only 20 pending join requests | Keep pagination (unbounded) but the app must page (Load more) or the product must cap group size. Decision needed |
| GET /activity-groups/{id}/templates | none enforced; realistic <10 | 1 single-page call (default 20) | Return whole list, like invites: service cap (e.g. 50) + a max templates per group at creation. Breaking change, coordinate with mobile |
| GET /sessions | none: a group's session history grows forever | Pages correctly (limit 50 + Load more) in MyActivities and group detail (when=upcoming/past); profile "joined sessions" one page of 20 | Keep pagination |
| GET /sessions/discover | none (radius-bound, count unbounded) | Pages (MyActivities limit 50 infinite); Home one page of 10 | Keep pagination |
| GET /activity-groups | none: all groups | ActivityGroupsScreen ONE page of 20, no Load more: "All groups" silently stops at 20; profile "groups" one page of 20 | Keep pagination; mobile gap: add Load more |
| GET /activity-groups/discover | none | Home one page of 50, no Load more | Keep pagination; mobile gap (or accept top 50) |
| GET /profiles | lookups: bounded by the ids/nickname sent; filter searches (city, country, age): unbounded | Only lookups: account_id (repeatable, whole roster in one call) and nickname. Reads items only, ignores next_page_token | Lookup by account_id must not page: return all requested (cap e.g. 200, 400 above it). Keep pagination for filter searches (the app does not use them). See bugs below |

CROSS-CUTTING FINDINGS (verified)
1. limit has NO upper bound. ParsePageParams only rejects negatives: limit=100000 is accepted everywhere; limit=0 means "no LIMIT" in the activity repositories (group, session, member, template, invite repos use `if filter.Limit > 0`), so ?limit=0 returns the whole table. Any authenticated caller can pull every group / session / member.
2. GET /profiles roster lookup is silently truncated. 25 account_ids with the default limit 20 returned 20 profiles + next_page_token (limit=0 or 100000 returned all 25). The app resolves a roster in one call and drops the token, so rosters over 20 show missing names. Attendees can be 200, group members unlimited.
3. GET /profiles?limit=N counts `limit` as a filter (query_params.go: `if q.Get("limit") != "" { hasFilter = true }`), so the "missing filter" guard is bypassed: GET /profiles?limit=100000 lists every profile (full name, date of birth, location, bio, interests) to any logged-in user.

Not paginated-by-design and unaffected: notifications retention exists (uvh) so that list is bounded.

title: Localization phase 2: mobile i18n foundation + auth module in en/hr
description:
Mobile app (../mobile-app) groundwork, proven end to end on one small module.
- Add i18next + react-i18next (Croatian needs one/few/other plurals via Intl.PluralRules, supported by Hermes) and expo-localization.

title: Localization: support multiple languages (backend + mobile app)
description:
## Goal
Let users use Rekreativko in their own language (en + hr first), built in small, shippable phases.

## Guiding rule
The backend returns codes and data; the client owns all in-app text. The backend only translates text delivered outside the app (email, SMS, later push). Already true for notifications (type + data) and partly for errors (AppError.code).

## Current state (2026-10-14 survey)
- Notifications: client builds the text from type + data (mobile-app modules/activity/utils/notifications.ts) - ready.
- Errors: AppError{code, message}; some screens map code to text, others show the English message.
- Activity types/levels: enum values, client can translate by value.
- Settings labels/descriptions: English strings in account-profile's account_settings_registry.go.
- Verification email/SMS: hardcoded English in shared/notification/service.go - the only text the backend must translate.
- Dates: toLocaleString(undefined, ...) follows the device, not the chosen language.
- preference.language setting exists (default en) but accepts any string and the app ignores it.
- Gateway already forwards Accept-Language; CORS allows it by default (safelisted header).

## Out of scope
User-written content (group names, bios, session descriptions); right-to-left languages.

## Open decisions
1. Languages: en + hr, or more (sr, de...)?
2. Who writes the Croatian text - the user, or Claude drafts it for review?
3. Default language for a new account: device language sent at sign-up (recommended) vs always en.

title: Measure session-details visibility cost before/after from activity logs
description: Confirm the effect of fgo/ezy/bgp: replay a session-details page open (8 requests) against the activity container built from HEAD and from the working tree, and count GetSession / EnsureSessionVisible log lines per request_id. title: Make session/group visibility relation check lazy
description: SessionService.GetSession evaluates isSessionRelated eagerly as an argument to Session.IsVisibleTo, so public sessions and the creator still pay 1-3 relation queries. Change IsVisibleTo to take func() bool. Same pattern in ActivityGroupService (activity_group_service.go isConfirmedMember).

title: Parity test: GetSession vs EnsureSessionVisible visibility
description: The visibility rule now lives in Go (Session.IsVisibleTo + isSessionRelated) and SQL (IsSessionVisibleTo). Add an integration test with a case matrix (public; private as creator, attendee, pending invite, expired invite, confirmed member, pending member, stranger; deleted session) asserting both paths agree.

title: Add single-query session visibility check for gate-only handlers
description: Opening session details triggers ~8 GetSession calls; 7 only gate visibility and discard the session, each costing 1 session load + 1-3 relation lookups. Add SessionRepository.IsSessionVisibleTo (one EXISTS query over session, session_attendee, session_invites, member) and SessionService.EnsureSessionVisible returning ErrSessionNotFound when not visible. Use it in the gate-only handlers (attendee_handler ListAttendees, team_formation_handler, team_formation_stream, team_voting_handler gate calls, team_draft_handler gate calls) and live hub dropRemovedViewer.
