title: Close team-formation SSE streams cleanly on activity shutdown
description: An SSE stream (GET /activity/api/v1/sessions/{id}/events) never ends on its own, so http.Server.Shutdown(5s) in activity waits the full grace period on every deploy and then cuts the streams abruptly. On shutdown the live.Hub should close every client with a new disconnect reason (e.g. server_shutdown) so the handler sends event: disconnected and phones reconnect to another instance right away. Hook it via srv.RegisterOnShutdown or by cancelling a base context before Shutdown. The gateway needs nothing: once activity ends the stream, the proxied request completes. Split out of the gateway timeout fix (step 4 of the plan).
close_reason: Hub.Shutdown closes SSE clients with server_shutdown via srv.RegisterOnShutdown; late connects rejected; tests + docs

title: Notify managers when team voting close hits a tie
description:
Mobile's team-formation notification list includes 'voting tied and needs a winner (organizer only)'. No event exists for it today: TeamVotingRound.Close returns a *TieError (409 tie_requires_winner) and the transaction rolls back, so nothing reaches the outbox. The organizer who pressed Close sees the 409 in-app, which is why 6gg.5 left this out.

Revisit if other managers (admins who didn't press Close) or a push notification need to know about the tie. Options: persist a voting.tie_requires_winner event on a separate transaction when Close hits a tie (dedupe per round and tied set), or have the client show the tie from GET /proposals. Then add a notifications consumer (team_voting_tied, screen team_voting, recipients = session managers).
close_reason: Tie notification: voting.tied event written in a second tx on TieError, deduped via last_tie_key, notifications consumer team_voting_tied for managers except the closer

title: Append-only domain event sink for history and analytics (NATS -> ClickHouse)
description: Durable, queryable history of every domain event, independent of Postgres: a NATS consumer subscribed to events.> writing each event (event_id, event_type, aggregate_id, occurred_at, payload) into an append-only store, deduplicated on event_id. ClickHouse is the likely store - depends on the assessment in rekreativko-api-u8y. This is where audit/reporting history lives once rows are hard-deleted or archived; note events are notification-shaped today, so decide whether key events (session.created/updated/cancelled, group.deleted) need fuller payloads to be useful as history. JetStream only retains 7 days, so the consumer must be durable and alert on lag. Effort: L.

title: Make soft-delete filters impossible to forget (live views or a shared base query)
description: Every read of a soft-deleted table must add deleted_at IS NULL by hand: activity session/group/member/template/attendee repos and account-profile profiles; rekreativko-api-dxp had to patch 5 session queries (GetSessionByID, ListSessions, DiscoverSessions, FindSessionsPastEndTime, ListActiveSessionIDsByGroup) and team_draft_repo/team_voting_repo still JOIN activity.session without it. Options: Postgres views (activity.live_session = SELECT ... WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) that repositories read from, or one shared base query/QueryBuilder helper per table. Also add partial indexes on the live rows (e.g. sessions WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Tables that move to archive tables (see the archive ticket in this epic) drop out of scope. Add an integration test per repository proving deleted rows never come back. Effort: M.

title: Purge published rows from every event_outbox table
description: identity, account-profile and activity each have <schema>.event_outbox; the outbox publisher only sets published_at and nothing ever deletes rows, so the tables grow forever and are not a real event history anyway (use the analytics sink in this epic for that). Add a periodic cleanup (outbox-publisher or the cron) that deletes rows with published_at older than a retention window (e.g. 7 days, matching the NATS stream MaxAge) and keeps failed_at rows (dead-lettered) until handled. Batch the deletes to avoid long locks; add an index on published_at if needed. Integration test per schema. Effort: S.
close_reason: Outbox purger deletes published rows older than retention (default 7d) in batches from every service schema; dead-lettered and pending rows kept; config, metric, README, unit + integration tests

title: Decide: do members keep past sessions of a deleted group in their history?
description: Product decision that drives how sessions are deleted. Today (rekreativko-api-dxp) deleting a group soft-deletes all its sessions, completed ones included, and they vanish everywhere - including a member's 'sessions I attended' (ListSessions attendee_id). Options: (a) past sessions stay visible in attendees' history (then sessions need soft delete or an archive table that history queries can read); (b) they disappear and only aggregated stats survive (then hard delete is fine, provided stats live in account-profile/session_statistics). Also decide for a cancelled group's past sessions. Output: the decision recorded in .claude/docs/activity.md, and the archive/soft-delete ticket in this epic updated accordingly.

title: Move deleted sessions (and other history rows) to archive tables instead of soft delete
description: Archive-table pattern: on delete, INSERT the row into e.g. activity.session_archive (same columns + deleted_at, deleted_by) and DELETE it from the live table in the same transaction, so live tables need no deleted_at filters and history stays complete and queryable. Start with activity.session (soft-deleted by DeleteGroupSessions since rekreativko-api-dxp); child rows (session_attendee, session_invites, session_team, drafts/picks, voting rounds/proposals/votes, session_statistics) reference session(id) without ON DELETE CASCADE, so decide per child table: archive alongside or delete. Evaluate the same for activity_group, member, session_template, session_attendee and account_profile.profiles, which also use deleted_at. Per project rule edit the existing 000001 migrations, no new migration files. Blocked by the history decision in this epic - if history is not needed, plain hard delete may be enough. Needs integration tests. Effort: L.

title: Data lifecycle: deletion, history and retention
description: Settle how the system deletes data and keeps history, per table instead of one global rule. Context (session 2026-09-27, after rekreativko-api-dxp added session.deleted_at): soft delete forced deleted_at IS NULL into 5 session queries and any forgotten filter leaks deleted rows; unique constraints need NULLS NOT DISTINCT workarounds. Replacing soft delete with 'hard delete + events as history' was rejected for now: NATS keeps events only 7 days (MaxAge in shared/events/nats_broker.go), outbox tables are a delivery queue not a queryable event store, and events are notification-shaped (e.g. session.cancelled has no title/time/location), so they can't reconstruct deleted state. Direction: hard-delete transient working state, keep soft delete (made safe) or archive tables where users see history or undo matters, send full event history to an analytics sink (ClickHouse, rekreativko-api-u8y), and purge published outbox rows.

title: Deleting an activity group leaves its scheduled/started sessions live
description: ActivityGroupService.DeleteActivityGroup soft-deletes the group but, unlike CancelActivityGroup (fixed in rekreativko-api-yeq), does not touch its sessions: scheduled/started sessions of a deleted group stay live and attendees are not told; running drafts/voting rounds keep going. The recurring-session cron already skips deleted groups (yeq). Decide whether delete should imply cancel (then reuse SessionService.CancelGroupSessions in the same transaction, as CancelActivityGroup does) or whether deleting a group that still has upcoming sessions should be rejected until it is cancelled. Needs an integration test. Effort: S.
close_reason: Group delete cancels live sessions then soft-deletes all group sessions (session.deleted_at, hidden from all reads)

title: End a running captain draft when its session is cancelled or completed
description: A captain draft (6gg.2) stays status in_progress if its session is cancelled (CancelSession, CancelFromGroup when the group is cancelled), completed (CompleteSession) or auto-completed by the cron (ExpireCompletedSessions). Picks are already refused (Pick checks the session status), but GET /sessions/{id}/draft keeps reporting a running draft with a current captain, which mobile would render as live. Fix: in those paths, cancel the active draft with a new reason (e.g. 'session_ended') under the session lock and emit draft.cancelled. Effort: S.
close_reason: Session cancel/complete/cron-expiry cancels a running draft and open voting round (session_ended) under the session lock

title: Bind outbox schema to the event writer at construction instead of passing it on every InsertEvents
description:
Every service writes domain events only to its own schema, yet domainevent.EventWriter.InsertEvents takes the schema on every call (~70 call sites across identity, account-profile, activity). It has already drifted: activity uses the activitySchema const but session_generator_service.go passes the literal "activity"; identity has its own 'const schema = "identity"'. The schema is also interpolated into SQL via %s, so validating it once at construction is safer than trusting every caller.

Proposal:
- Split the writer from the reader. Writer: domainevent.NewEventWriter(txManager, schema) bound in each service's cmd/*/main.go (activity api + cron, identity, account-profile); InsertEvents(ctx, events ...Event) with no schema arg. Validate the schema identifier once in the constructor.
- Keep the reader side (ReadEvents, MarkEventAsPublished, MarkEventAsFailed) schema-parameterized - the outbox-publisher legitimately iterates OUTBOX_SCHEMAS.
- Make InsertEvents variadic so services can collect events from several aggregates and insert them in one call (e.g. SessionService.CreateTeams currently loops over attendees then inserts session events separately).
- Remove the per-service schema constants (activitySchema, identity 'schema') and the "activity" literal.
- Update integration tests that construct NewDomainEventManager.

Effort: M (mechanical, touches all three writing services + tests).
acceptance_criteria: No InsertEvents call passes a schema; each service binds its schema once in main.go; outbox-publisher unchanged in behavior; all unit and integration tests pass

title: Fix failing shared/config Test_config_Load (GATEWAY_API_KEY required)
description: Test_config_Load/should_load_config_from_environment_variables fails with: 'required key GATEWAY_API_KEY missing value'. The test does not set GATEWAY_API_KEY, which the shared Config now requires. Reproduces on clean HEAD (b1483c8), independent of team work. Fix: set the env var in the test (or make the test derive required keys). Related to shared-config coupling in rekreativko-api-uo5.
close_reason: Test_config_Load sets the required GATEWAY_API_KEY, GATEWAY_API_KEYS and OUTBOX_SCHEMAS env vars

title: Fix failing SessionTemplateRepository integration tests (location_city NOT NULL)
description: Pre-existing on main (verified on clean HEAD): go test -tags=integration ./activity/internal/infrastructure/persistence fails 7 TestSessionTemplateRepository_* tests (CreateAndGet, Update, Delete, Query, FindRecurringTemplatesToGenerate, UpdateGeneratedUpTo, ConcurrentAccess) with 'null value in column location_city of relation session_template violates not-null constraint (SQLSTATE 23502)'. The SessionTemplateBuilder fixtures don't set location by default (locationCity/locationCountry are nil pointers) while the schema requires them.
close_reason: SessionTemplateBuilder defaults to a location (schema requires it); Update test passes the existing location instead of nil

title: Device token registration API (notifications service)
description: Table + endpoints to register/update/unregister a device push token per account and device (platform, token, last_seen). Unregister on logout. Routed through the gateway; auth required.
acceptance_criteria: Mobile can register and unregister tokens; multiple devices per account; tokens removed on logout
notes: 2026-10-03: provider not decided yet (comparison in rekreativko-api-79p.2 notes; leaning Expo push service). This API doesn't need to wait for it: store provider (expo|fcm|apns) + platform with each token so the provider can change later without a data migration.

title: Push delivery via provider (notifications service)
description: Decide provider (Expo push service vs FCM/APNs). Sender consumes notification events, sends to all of a user's devices, handles receipts, retries, and removes invalid tokens. Respect existing notification preferences if any.
acceptance_criteria: A notification event results in a push on registered devices; invalid tokens cleaned up; failures observable via metrics/logs
notes:
Provider comparison (2026-10-03, NOT decided - deferred, push isn't needed for the app to work yet; mobile's a01.10 waits on this epic):

Expo push service
- App sends one token type: ExponentPushToken[...] (expo-notifications gives it directly)
- Backend: one HTTPS API for iOS + Android
- Credentials: APNs/FCM keys uploaded once to Expo (EAS); backend holds none
- Invalid tokens: Expo push receipts report DeviceNotRegistered
- Mobile work: smallest
- Trade-off: depends on Expo's service, less low-level control

FCM (+ APNs) directly
- App sends native FCM / APNs tokens
- Backend: FCM API, plus APNs or FCM's iOS bridge
- Credentials: backend holds the Firebase service account (and APNs key)
- Invalid tokens: FCM/APNs error responses
- Mobile work: Firebase setup in the app
- Trade-off: more control, more setup on both sides

Leaning: Expo push service - least work for both teams, fits the Expo app. Keep it switchable: 79p.1 stores provider + platform per token, so moving to FCM later means a new sender, not a data migration. (General knowledge, not checked against current Expo/FCM docs or pricing.)

title: Mobile push notification infrastructure
description:
Platform feature, not team-specific. Neither backend nor the mobile app has push today: the app has no expo-notifications or push setup, and the notifications service only has an SMS sender. Team formation ships without it (live updates via SSE while app is open); push adds background delivery for e.g. "your turn to pick".

Backend scope: device-token storage + register/unregister API, provider integration (decision needed: Expo push service since the app is Expo, vs FCM/APNs directly), sender that turns notification events into pushes, receipt/invalid-token handling.
Mobile scope (their tickets): permissions, token registration, foreground/background handling, deep links.
Once done, team formation notifications (rekreativko-api-6gg.5) can also be pushed.

title: account-profile: treat 'profile exists' as idempotent success when account.verified event is redelivered
description:
account-profile/internal/interfaces/events/account_verified_handler.go creates the profile and settings in one transaction. account_profile.profiles has account_id as PRIMARY KEY, so a redelivered identity.account.verified event hits a unique violation, which is mapped to ErrAccountProfileExists (profile_exists conflict). The handler returns that as an error, so the broker Naks and redelivers up to MaxDeliver=3, then Terms the message and logs errors. No duplicate data is written (the tx rolls back), but a normal at-least-once redelivery is reported as a failure and produces error noise and wasted retries.

Fix direction: in createProfileEventHandler.Handle, treat ErrAccountProfileExists (and the equivalent settings conflict) as success (log at debug and return nil), or make CreateAccountProfile/CreateSettings use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Careful that a partially-existing state (profile exists but settings missing) is still repaired - check both independently rather than swallowing all conflicts. Add a unit test with fakes for redelivery, and an integration test if the repository SQL changes.

Found while checking other consumers after fixing the notifications idempotency bug. Effort: S.
close_reason: Profile/settings creation idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING); redelivered account.verified succeeds and repairs missing settings

title: NATS consumers drop messages after MaxDeliver=3 with no dead-letter path
description:
shared/events/nats_broker.go configures durable consumers with MaxDeliver: 3 and AckWait 30s. When a handler fails and max deliveries is reached, the message is Term()'d (around lines 252-276) with only an error log. There is no dead-letter stream/subject, no persisted record of what was dropped, and no replay mechanism. Any event whose handler fails 3 times (e.g. a DB outage longer than the redelivery window in notifications or account-profile) is permanently lost, so users silently miss notifications or never get an account profile created.

This is the consumer-side counterpart of the outbox poison-pill fix (rekreativko-api-tqr), which dead-letters on the producer side via retry_count/failed_at. Idempotent handlers (rekreativko-api-m8j) make redelivery safe but do not prevent loss after the third failure.

Design questions: (a) publish terminated messages to a DLQ subject/stream (e.g. dlq.<subject>) with the original payload, error and delivery count, (b) add a redelivery BackOff instead of the fixed AckWait so transient outages outlast 3 attempts, (c) metrics/alert on terminated messages, (d) a way to replay from the DLQ. Distinguish permanent errors (decode failures - Term immediately, straight to DLQ) from transient ones (retry with backoff). Effort: M.
close_reason: Added DLQ stream (dlq.>) in shared/events/nats_broker.go: messages are dead-lettered with failure headers after max deliveries or on permanent errors (decode failures marked via events.Permanent), retries use NakWithDelay, metric events_dead_lettered_total. Unit + real-NATS integration tests. Follow-up hardening in rekreativko-api-755.

title: Introduce interfaces for concrete dependencies in application services so they can be unit tested
description:
Application services depend on the concrete *postgres.TransactionManager (shared/store/postgres), so service methods like AttendeeService.CreateRSVP cannot be unit-tested with mocked repositories without a real database. Found while fixing rekreativko-api-yd6 (no test could be added). Related to rekreativko-api-tf6 (no unit tests for activity domain/application layer) - this is a prerequisite for it.

Scope: go service by service and replace concrete types with small consumer-side interfaces (defined in the application package). Main offender is *postgres.TransactionManager, used as txManager in: activity application (attendee, session, session_template, session_generator, invite, member, activity_group services), account-profile application (account_profile_service, account_settings_service) and events handlers (account_verified_handler, subscriber), identity application/service.go, notifications application/notification_service.go, and shared/domainevent/domain_event.go. Some services also call txManager.Querier(ctx) directly (e.g. AttendeeService.lockSessionCapacity runs pg_advisory_xact_lock), so that needs to be abstracted behind an interface method or a separate locker port. Also audit each service for other concrete deps (*metrics.Metrics, *logger.Logger, telemetry) that block testing.

Suggested approach: define a minimal TxManager interface (WithTransaction(ctx, func(ctx) error) error, plus Querier if unavoidable) - ideally once in shared - have the concrete postgres.TransactionManager satisfy it, and add a fake for tests. Do it per service in separate commits, starting with activity (attendee_service, session_service). Persistence-layer repos can keep the concrete type (they need real DB integration tests). Effort: M-L.

Acceptance: application services accept interfaces for tx manager; at least one unit test per service using mocked repos + fake tx manager proves it works (e.g. CreateRSVP membership lookup error propagation from yd6).

title: Investigate ClickHouse adoption for the project
description: A senior engineer should investigate how ClickHouse could be used in this project and for what use cases (e.g. analytics/reporting, event/metrics storage, large-scale read-heavy query workloads currently served by PostgreSQL). Deliverable: an assessment of concrete use cases where ClickHouse would be a good fit here, how it would fit into the existing architecture (modular monolith with shared PostgreSQL, NATS event-driven communication, outbox pattern), and a recommendation on whether/where to adopt it.

title: Add forward geocoding (city/country/street -> lat/long) to location service
description: The location service (rekreativko-api-bog) currently only implements reverse geocoding. Mobile's web target still calls Nominatim directly for forward geocoding (nominatimForwardGeocode in its location client, used by Session/Session Template location fields to resolve a typed city/street into coordinates) - that direct third-party call is not yet covered by the new backend proxy/cache. Follow-up: add a forward-geocoding endpoint (structured city+country search, plus free-text search when a street is given) to the location service, mirroring the caching/rate-limiting approach already built for reverse geocoding, so mobile can drop its last direct Nominatim dependency.
close_reason: Added forward-geocoding endpoint (GET /api/v1/geocode/forward) to the location service, mirroring reverse-geocode caching/rate-limiting: structured city+country search, free-text search when street is given, Postgres cache table, shared Nominatim rate limiter, new unlabeled cache-hit/miss counters (no cardinality risk), swagger docs regenerated.

title: Shared Config struct forces every service to supply env vars for unrelated services, undermining independent deployability
description: shared/config/config.go defines one flat Config struct embedding ServiceConfig, GatewayServiceConfig, IdentityServiceConfig, AccountProfileServiceConfig, ActivityServiceConfig, NotificationsServiceConfig, Outbox, NatsConfig, JWT, etc., and every service binary (gateway, identity, account-profile, activity, notifications, outbox-publisher/cmd/worker) calls the same config.Load() which runs envconfig.Process("", &c) against the entire struct. Several fields are marked required:"true" globally regardless of which service actually uses them, e.g. GatewayServiceConfig.GatewayKeys (env GATEWAY_API_KEYS - only meaningfully used by the gateway binary to build its outbound X-Gateway-Key value) and Outbox.Schemas (env OUTBOX_SCHEMAS - only used by outbox-publisher/cmd/worker). Because envconfig.Process fails fast on any missing required field, this means e.g. the identity service cannot start without GATEWAY_API_KEYS and OUTBOX_SCHEMAS set in its environment, even though identity's own code never reads either value. This directly contradicts CLAUDE.md's stated architecture ('Each service can run independently...') and adds operational friction: every new required field added for one service's config leaks into every other service's required environment, and it's easy to forget which fields are actually load-bearing for a given binary. Suggested approach: split Config into a small shared 'common' struct (Service, Logger, Server, Postgres, Redis, JWT, Telemetry - the genuinely cross-cutting concerns) plus per-binary structs that each cmd/*/main.go loads separately (e.g. config.LoadGateway(), config.LoadIdentity()), so each service's required env vars match what it actually needs. Effort: M (touches every cmd/*/main.go).

title: Root CLAUDE.md Service Structure section is stale - omits activity (the CORE domain) and notifications services
description: The 'Service Structure' section of the root CLAUDE.md only lists Gateway (8080), Identity (8081), Account Profile (8082), and the Outbox Publisher. It does not mention the activity service (which .claude/docs/activity.md calls out as the 'CORE part of the application', with its own cmd/api and cmd/cron entry points, ~24k lines including migrations, and the largest domain/application layer in the repo) or the notifications service (which has its own full DDD layer set and is routed by the gateway in gateway/internal/router.go and gateway/cmd/api/main.go's serviceConfig map). Same gap in the 'Adding a New Service' checklist and the general architecture description, which still describes only a 3-service-plus-outbox topology. Anyone (human or agent) reading CLAUDE.md to get an overview before working in this repo will miss that activity and notifications exist at all, contradicting the instruction to 'get an overview first' - the doc that's supposed to enable that is itself incomplete. Suggested approach: update the Service Structure list to include activity (8083?) and notifications (8084?) with their actual ports/responsibilities, and mention activity/cmd/cron (the session-template generation cron job) since it's a distinct deployable not covered anywhere in CLAUDE.md's Development Commands section either. Effort: S (documentation only).

title: Application layer repository interfaces depend on infrastructure/persistence Filter types (inverted dependency), plus dead duplicate Filter types in identity
description: Across all three services (identity/internal/application/service.go, account-profile/internal/application/account_profile_service.go, and all of activity/internal/application/*.go via repositories.go), the application-layer repository interfaces are defined against filter/query DTOs that live in the infrastructure/persistence package (e.g. persistence.AccountFilter, persistence.RefreshTokenFilter, persistence.VerificationCodeFilter), and every application file imports .../internal/infrastructure/persistence directly to reference them. In a hexagonal/DDD layering, the application layer should own the port (interface + its parameter types) and infrastructure should depend on application, not the reverse - here the dependency arrow points the wrong way, and it's consistent enough across all three services that it looks like an intentional convention rather than an accident, but it still means application code can never be compiled/tested without pulling in the concrete persistence package. Separately, identity/internal/application/service.go additionally defines its own AccountFilter, RefreshTokenFilter, and VerificationCodeFilter structs (lines ~47-59) that appear to be unused dead code - grep shows zero references to application.AccountFilter etc. anywhere in the codebase, while the interfaces actually in use (accountReaderWriter.GetBy, refreshTokenReaderWriter.GetTokenBy, etc.) take the persistence.* versions instead. Suggested approach: move the Filter DTOs into the application package (or a shared query-params location each service owns) so infrastructure implements against application-defined ports; separately, delete the unused duplicate Filter structs in identity/internal/application/service.go once confirmed unused, or wire them up if they were meant to replace the persistence ones. Effort: M (touches all three services' repo interfaces and their infra implementations).

title: Public-route allowlist for gateway auth is defined twice and can drift
description: The set of unauthenticated identity endpoints (login/register/verify-account/resend-verification-code/refresh-token) is hardcoded as a regex in two independent places: (1) gateway/cmd/api/main.go's publicPaths slice, consumed by middleware.NewAuthMiddleware(...).RequireAuth which runs first in the middleware chain and short-circuits auth entirely for matches; (2) gateway/internal/router.go's loadRoutes(), inside the '/identity' Route's AuthRule with RequireAuth:false, consumed later by Router.isAuthSatisfied. Both lists already differ in content (main.go's list also includes /swagger/.* and /health, router.go's doesn't need to since those aren't proxied routes) which makes it easy to lose track of which list is authoritative. Because AuthMiddleware runs before the router in the chain, router.go's AuthRule.RequireAuth:false is currently mostly redundant/defense-in-depth, but that isn't documented anywhere, so a future contributor adding a new public endpoint could easily update one list and not the other - either accidentally leaving a route behind auth that should be public, or (worse) believing a route is protected because it's marked RequireAuth:true in router.go when AuthMiddleware already let it through unauthenticated. Suggested approach: derive one list from the other (e.g. have main.go build publicPaths from router.NewRouter()'s routes instead of a separate literal), or extract the identity public-path regex into one shared constant/var referenced by both call sites. Effort: S.
close_reason: Public gateway routes declared once on router AuthRules; main.go builds AuthMiddleware publicPaths from Router.PublicPaths(); dropped dead /health and /swagger entries; agreement test added

title: Domain layer in identity and account-profile depends on infrastructure (pgx) and app-layer concerns (domainerror), unlike activity
description: identity/internal/domain/errors.go and account-profile/internal/domain/errors.go both import github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 directly and implement MapErrToAppError(err error) *domainerror.AppError inside the domain package - mapping domain sentinel errors to an HTTP-status-aware AppError DTO and even special-casing the infra-specific pgx.ErrNoRows sentinel. This violates the DDD dependency rule documented in CLAUDE.md (domain should not depend on infrastructure/interfaces) and couples the domain package to both a specific SQL driver and an HTTP-facing error shape. Notably this is inconsistent across the three services: activity does this correctly - its equivalent MapErrToAppError (and the pgx import) lives in activity/internal/application/error_mapper.go, in the application layer, not domain. Suggested approach: move MapErrToAppError out of identity/internal/domain/errors.go and account-profile/internal/domain/errors.go into a new identity/internal/application/error_mapper.go and account-profile/internal/application/error_mapper.go respectively (mirroring activity's existing pattern), keeping only the plain errors.New(...) sentinels and any pure-domain error types in the domain package. Effort: S per service (mechanical move + import fixups).

title: No unit tests for activity domain/application layer (core domain)
description: activity/internal/domain and activity/internal/application have zero *_test.go files (find activity/internal/application -name '*_test.go' and find activity/internal/domain -name '*_test.go' both return nothing), despite the activity bounded context being called out in .claude/docs/activity.md and CLAUDE.md as the CORE domain of the system. Commit 36cb6607 added substantial, intricate business logic here with no accompanying tests, e.g.: capacity-aware RSVP with waitlist promotion and approval-gated join requests (activity/internal/application/attendee_service.go CreateRSVP/ApproveAttendee/promoteNextPending), session visibility rules mixing public/private/group-membership/attendee checks (session_service.go GetSession/isSessionRelated, ListSessions filter building), session cancellation with attendee fan-out (resolveSessionAttendeeUserIDs), and the cron-driven ExpireCompletedSessions. These paths have subtle edge cases (capacity race re-checks, waitlist ordering, visibility fallback logic) that are exactly the kind of logic regressions slip into silently without tests. Suggest adding table-driven unit tests for the domain invariants (activity/internal/domain/*.go) and service-level tests (with repo interfaces mocked) for the application layer, starting with attendee_service.go and session_service.go given their size and complexity.

title: Access log now logs full raw query string on every request
description: shared/middleware/logging.go's Logging middleware was changed in commit 36cb6607 to add "query_params", r.URL.RawQuery to the structured fields logged on every request (see the 'fields := []any{...}' block). This logs the entire raw query string verbatim for every request at INFO/WARN/ERROR level, with no allowlist/redaction of sensitive parameter names. There is currently no endpoint that puts secrets in a query string, but nothing prevents one being added later (e.g. a password-reset or magic-link GET endpoint with a token=... param, or a search endpoint that echoes free-text PII), and it would then be silently written to logs (which may be shipped to Loki/long-term storage per observability/loki/loki-config.yaml) without anyone noticing, since the middleware is generic and applies everywhere. Suggest redacting known-sensitive query keys (token, code, password, secret, key) before logging, or documenting query strings as an explicit no-secrets zone enforced by review.
close_reason: Access log and trace http.target redact query values except an allowlist (loggedQueryKeys); unknown params keep their name and show [redacted]; unparseable queries are not logged

title: Localization phase 5: stored language for messages sent without a request (push, reminders)
description:
Deferred until push notifications or scheduled reminders exist. Messages sent later, with no request to take the language from, need the recipient's stored preference.language.
- account-profile publishes an event when preference.language changes (e.g. account_profile.settings.language_changed, via the outbox).
- The consumer (notifications service) keeps its own copy of each account's language and renders push text in it.
Don't build until there is a consumer - until then nothing reads it.

title: Publishing an activity group raises an event typed activity.group.updated
description: ActivityGroup.Activate raises ActivityPublishedEvent, but NewActivityPublishedEvent (domain/events.go) sets EventType to EventActivityGroupUpdated - there is no 'published' event type, so a consumer cannot tell a publish from an edit. Meanwhile EventActivityGroupStarted / NewActivityStartedEvent exist but nothing raises them. Nobody subscribes to activity.group.* today, so nothing breaks; decide whether publish needs its own type (e.g. activity.group.published) or the unused 'started' event should be removed. Found while writing tests for tf6.

title: Member: two unused CanReJoin methods disagree - remove or reconcile
description: domain/member.go has MemberStatus.CanReJoin (true for left and rejected) and Member.CanReJoin (true for left and removed). Neither is called anywhere outside tests, and they contradict each other (a rejected person can 'rejoin' by one, a removed person by the other). Rejoining actually goes through MemberService.RequestToJoinGroup, which only refuses pending/confirmed members (ErrAlreadyParticipating). Decide the intended rule (can someone who was removed or rejected ask again?), then delete the dead methods or make one authoritative and use it there. Found while writing tests for tf6.

title: Keep long-lived SSE streams out of request-duration metrics
description: The logging/metrics/tracing middlewares (shared/middleware) record request duration for every request. A team-formation SSE stream can stay open for tens of minutes, so each one lands in the HTTP latency histogram (gateway and activity) as a huge outlier and skews p95/p99. Either skip the duration observation for stream routes or add a stream=true label. The single access-log line written when a stream ends is still useful and should stay. Split out of the gateway timeout fix (step 5 of the plan).
close_reason: SSE responses are counted but skipped in duration/size histograms (middleware.Metrics skips text/event-stream)

title: Hard-delete finished transient rows (answered/expired invites and similar)
description: Some tables hold short-lived working state with no lasting value once finished; draft picks and voting proposals/votes are already deleted when a draft/round ends (D16). Candidates to purge after a grace period: activity.group_invites and activity.session_invites that are accepted/declined/expired, drafts and voting rounds of long-completed sessions (keep the result via the session's teams). Implement as a cron step (activity/cmd/cron) deleting rows older than N days, with the history kept by domain events (see the event-sink ticket in this epic). Confirm nothing (UI, stats) reads old invites first. Effort: S.

title: Broker: harden dead-letter publish failure path (retry DLQ publish, log payload, alert)
description:
Follow-up to rekreativko-api-wpn. In shared/events/nats_broker.go, deadLetter() publishes a failed message to the DLQ stream once. If that publish fails (NATS flap, stream misconfigured), the failure is logged with the stream sequence and counted in events_dead_lettered_total{dlq_published="false"}, and the message is still Term()'d. The payload is NOT in the log; the message is only recoverable from the EVENTS stream by sequence (nats stream get EVENTS <seq>) while it is inside EVENTS retention (7 days / 1GB).

Improvements (a DB table was considered and rejected: handlers usually fail because the DB is down, so a DB fallback would fail in the same outage, and it would add a DB dependency to the shared broker plus a table/migration per service):
1. Retry the DLQ publish 2-3 times with a short delay before giving up, to cover brief NATS flaps. Keep it bounded so a dead broker cannot stall the consumer loop.
2. On final failure, log the payload (truncated) together with the stream sequence, so the message can be reconstructed after EVENTS retention expires. Decide whether payloads are acceptable in logs (events mostly carry IDs but may contain user data); redact or hash if not.
3. Add a Prometheus alert rule (observability/) on events_dead_lettered_total{dlq_published="false"} > 0, since it means the safety net failed and the 7-day recovery window is running.
4. Extend the unit test with a fake DLQ that fails N times then succeeds.

Known related gap, not covered here: if a consumer crashes on every delivery, the server exhausts MaxDeliver without processMessage running, so nothing reaches the DLQ; catching that needs a subscription to the $JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.CONSUMER.MAX_DELIVERIES advisory.

Only worth a durable store beyond this if the events become business-critical; then prefer a transactional inbox table written by the handler in the same tx as the business change. Effort: S.

title: Activity Catalog bounded context is a hardcoded shared enum, not the documented admin-managed aggregate
description: .claude/docs/arhitecture.md documents a dedicated 'Activity Catalog Context' with its own aggregate (ActivityType: name, description) and use cases ('List activity types', 'Create activity type - admin'), explicitly 'does not know about users, groups and events'. The actual implementation instead defines activity types as a closed, hardcoded Go enum in shared/activitycatalog/activity_type.go (ActivityType string constants + a validActivityTypes map), consumed directly by both account-profile's interests and activity's groups. There is no database table, no admin CRUD API, no per-type metadata (description, icon/category, locale strings), and no way to add or retire an activity type without a code change and redeploy of every service that imports shared/activitycatalog. This works fine at the current small, fixed list size, but it's a real extension point implied directly by the existing docs and code structure (the comment in activity_type.go even says 'single source of truth ... shared across bounded contexts', i.e. it already plays the catalog's role, just without persistence or admin management). Suggested approach: if/when the activity type list needs to grow or vary by market/locale, promote shared/activitycatalog into a real small service (or a table owned by one existing service, e.g. activity) with a simple admin-only CRUD endpoint, keeping the shared Go package as a typed client/cache in front of it rather than the source of truth. Effort: L (new bounded context) - flagging as an opportunity, not urgent, since the current static list satisfies today's needs.
